# `modules/EditorAudio.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/modules/EditorAudio.js`

EditorAudio.js - Simulation Audio Bridge for the Editor Manages the runtime AudioEngine lifecycle during play mode: - Initializes AudioEngine on first play - Ticks audio each frame while playing - Stops all sim audio on stop/pause - Bridges substance emitters → procedural audio

## Functions

### `async startSimAudio(editor)`

Called when user enters play mode. Initializes engine if needed and starts audio.

**Parameters:**

- `editor` *(Object)* — EditorApp instance

### `stopSimAudio()`

Called when user exits play mode (Stop). Stops all active sources with a short fade.

### `pauseSimAudio()`

Called when user pauses. Suspends the AudioContext (freezes all audio in place).

### `async resumeSimAudio()`

Called when user resumes from pause.

### `tickSimAudio(dt)`

Tick the audio engine. Call once per frame while playing.

**Parameters:**

- `dt` *(number)* — Frame delta in seconds

### `destroySimAudio()`

Full cleanup. Call on editor close.

### `getSimAudioEngine()`

Get the current engine instance (for external integration).

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```
